database_name: OPD Java Indonesia - Pre-Round History Taking Question Bank

diseases.name_en: Acute Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Common Cold)
diseases.name_id: Infeksi Saluran Pernapasan Atas Akut (ISPA)/Common Cold
diseases.context_note: Consistently the #1 or #2 outpatient diagnosis at Puskesmas across Java (Jakarta, Central & West Java data); driven by crowding, poor ventilation, tropical climate/pollution.
red_flags: Stridor or drooling in a child

questions.q: When did the symptoms start, and did they come on suddenly or gradually?
Is the nasal discharge clear/watery or thick and colored (yellow/green)?
questions.purpose: Distinguish viral vs possible secondary bacterial infection

questions.q: Do you have a fever? If yes, how high and for how long?
Is there any shortness of breath, chest pain, or wheezing?
questions.purpose: Screen for lower respiratory involvement (pneumonia, asthma)

questions.q: Do you have ear pain or reduced hearing?
questions.purpose: Screen for otitis media as a complication

questions.q: Have you been in contact with anyone with similar symptoms recently?
Do you smoke, or is anyone in your household a smoker?
questions.purpose: Identify irritant exposure and risk of prolonged symptoms

questions.q: Do you have any chronic lung disease, heart disease, or immune-suppressing condition?
Have you tried any medication already? Did it help?
questions.purpose: Guide further management, avoid duplicate therapy

diseases.context_note: Among the top 3 outpatient diagnoses in Jakarta puskesmas (283,000+ visits in 2024); a major NCD burden across Java.

questions.q: Have you had your blood pressure checked before, and if so, what were the readings?
Are you currently taking any regular medication, and if so, what is it for and how consistently do you take it?
Do you have headaches, dizziness, or blurred vision?
Do you experience chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath, especially on exertion?
Does anyone in your family have a history of high blood pressure readings, stroke, or heart disease?
How much salty food do you typically eat, and do you smoke or drink alcohol?
Do you have diabetes, high cholesterol, or kidney disease?
Have you had any swelling in your legs or changes in how much you urinate?
questions.purpose: Screen for heart failure or renal involvement

questions.q: Do you check your blood pressure at home? What are typical readings?

diseases.context_note: Ranked top 3 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas 2024 (202,882 visits); reflects poor oral hygiene access.
red_flags: Facial swelling spreading to eye/neck (risk of cellulitis)

questions.q: Which tooth or area is painful, and how long has the pain been present?
Is the pain constant or does it come and go? Is it worse with hot, cold, or sweet food?
Does the pain wake you up at night or get worse when lying down?
Is there any swelling of the face or gums?
Do you have a fever or feel generally unwell?
questions.purpose: Screen for systemic spread of infection

questions.q: Have you had any recent dental treatment or trauma to the tooth?
Do you have difficulty opening your mouth or swallowing?

diseases.context_note: One of the top outpatient complaints across Java puskesmas ('sakit maag'); linked to irregular meals, spicy food, stress, H. pylori prevalence.

questions.q: Where exactly is the discomfort, and does it relate to eating (before, during, or after meals)?
How long have you had these symptoms, and are they constant or intermittent?
Have you noticed any weight loss, difficulty swallowing, or vomiting blood/black stools?
questions.purpose: Screen for alarm features requiring urgent referral/endoscopy

questions.q: Do you regularly take NSAIDs, aspirin, steroids, or herbal/jamu preparations?
How would you describe your eating pattern - do you often skip meals, eat late, or eat spicy/fatty food?
Do you smoke or drink coffee/alcohol regularly?
Is the pain related to stress or does it improve with antacids?
questions.purpose: Support functional dyspepsia vs organic cause

questions.q: Does anyone in your family have a history of stomach problems, ulcers, or stomach cancer?

diseases.context_note: Top 5 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas (188,000+ visits, 2024); rising prevalence across urban and rural Java.
red_flags: Very high or very low glucose with symptoms
Non-healing foot ulcer with signs of infection
Rapid unexplained weight loss with vomiting

questions.q: Have you ever been told your blood sugar was high, and are you currently on any treatment related to that?
Do you experience excessive thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss?
Do you check your blood sugar at home? What are your recent readings?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or pain in your feet, or any wounds that are slow to heal?
Have you had any changes in your vision recently?
Does anyone in your family have a history of high blood sugar problems?
What does your diet typically look like, and how physically active are you?
Do you have high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or any history of heart or kidney problems?
Are you taking your medications regularly, and have you had any episodes of very low blood sugar (shakiness, sweating, confusion)?

diseases.context_note: Top 6 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas 2024 (108,167 visits); complication of poorly controlled chronic hypertension.
red_flags: Chest pain suggestive of acute coronary syndrome

questions.q: How long have you had high blood pressure, and has it been well controlled?
Do you get short of breath with activity, or when lying flat at night?
Have you noticed swelling in your legs or ankles?
questions.purpose: Screen for fluid overload/right heart strain

questions.q: Do you have chest pain or tightness, and does it relate to exertion?
questions.purpose: Screen for concurrent ischemic heart disease

questions.q: Do you wake up at night gasping for breath or needing extra pillows to sleep?
Are you taking your prescribed medications regularly?
Do you have diabetes, high cholesterol, or a history of kidney disease?
Have you had any palpitations or episodes of dizziness/fainting?

diseases.context_note: Top 7 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas 2024; usually detected on routine screening rather than symptoms.
symptoms: Occasionally associated with early cardiovascular symptoms
red_flags: Calf pain with walking (peripheral artery disease)
Very high triglycerides with abdominal pain (pancreatitis risk)

questions.q: Have you had any blood tests done before, and if so, were any results outside the normal range?
Does anyone in your family have a history of early heart attack or stroke?
What does your typical diet look like - fried foods, fatty meats, coconut milk (santan)?
questions.purpose: Identify dietary contributors common in Javanese cuisine

questions.q: Do you exercise regularly?
Do you have diabetes, hypertension, or thyroid problems?
Are you currently taking any regular medication, and have you noticed any muscle pain since starting any new medication?
questions.purpose: Assess treatment and statin side effects

questions.q: Do you smoke or drink alcohol?

diseases.context_note: Frequently reported as 'nyeri sendi/rematik' - among the most common OPD diagnoses at rural Java puskesmas (e.g., top diagnosis at Puskesmas Gabus II 2023).
symptoms: Stiffness, worse in the morning or after rest
red_flags: Joint swelling with redness and warmth (possible septic arthritis/gout flare)
Symmetric small joint swelling (possible rheumatoid arthritis)

questions.q: Which muscles or joints are affected, and is it one-sided or both sides?
How long have you had this pain, and did it start suddenly or gradually?
Is there any swelling, redness, or warmth over the joint?
questions.purpose: Screen for inflammatory or infectious arthritis

questions.q: Is the stiffness worse in the morning, and how long does it last?
Does activity make it better or worse?
questions.purpose: Differentiate mechanical (worse with use) vs inflammatory (better with use)

questions.q: Have you had any recent injury, unusual physical activity, or repetitive strain?
Do you have fever, weight loss, or fatigue along with the pain?
Have you had similar sudden joint pain episodes before, especially in your big toe or another single joint?

diseases.context_note: Consistently in the top 10 across Jakarta and rural Java puskesmas; linked to food/water sanitation.
red_flags: Signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, lethargy, no urine output, very dry mouth)
High fever with severe abdominal pain

questions.q: How many times a day are you passing loose stools, and since when?
Is there any blood or mucus in the stool?
Do you have fever, vomiting, or abdominal cramping?
Have you eaten any food or water from a questionable source recently, or eaten out?
Are you able to keep fluids down, and how much are you urinating?
Is anyone else at home or nearby with similar symptoms?
Have you traveled recently or taken any antibiotics recently?
Do you feel dizzy when standing, or notice a very dry mouth?

diseases.context_note: Listed among Jakarta's top-10 outpatient puskesmas diagnoses (2024); urban Java has established ART programs.
red_flags: Signs of opportunistic infection (severe cough, neurological symptoms, severe thrush)

questions.q: Have you ever been tested for any infections that affect the immune system, and do you know the results?
Have you had any risk exposures - unprotected sex, shared needles, blood transfusion?
questions.purpose: Assess risk factors (asked with sensitivity and confidentiality)

questions.q: Have you had recurrent fevers, weight loss, or night sweats?
questions.purpose: Screen for constitutional symptoms of HIV progression

questions.q: Have you noticed white patches in your mouth or frequent skin infections?
Are you currently taking any regular medication for immune system support, and do you take it consistently?
Have you had any cough lasting more than 2 weeks?
questions.purpose: Screen for TB co-infection, common in Indonesia

questions.q: Has your partner or anyone close to you been diagnosed with a condition that affects the immune system?
questions.purpose: Assess household/partner context and need for partner testing

diseases.context_note: Indonesia has one of the world's highest TB burdens; consistently appears in top-10 puskesmas diagnoses across Java (rural and urban).
red_flags: Signs of disseminated/miliary TB (very unwell, altered consciousness)
Known HIV-positive with TB symptoms (urgent workup)

questions.q: How long have you had a cough, and has it changed in character?
questions.purpose: Screen duration - >2 weeks triggers TB workup per national guidelines

questions.q: Have you coughed up blood or blood-streaked sputum?
questions.purpose: Assess for hemoptysis, a red flag

questions.q: Do you have fevers, especially at night, or night sweats?
Have you lost weight recently without trying?
Has anyone you live with or spend a lot of time with had a long-lasting cough or been treated for a lung infection recently?
Have you ever been treated for a long-term lung infection before, and did you complete the full course of treatment?
questions.purpose: Screen for relapse or drug-resistant TB risk

questions.q: Have you ever been tested for any condition that weakens your immune system?
questions.purpose: Assess co-infection risk, affects management urgency

questions.q: Do you live in a crowded household, or work/live in close quarters with others?
Have you had chest pain or shortness of breath?

diseases.context_note: Java experiences seasonal dengue outbreaks (rainy season); a frequent cause of acute febrile OPD presentation.
symptoms: Mild bleeding gums or easy bruising
red_flags: Bleeding (gums, nose, black stool, heavy menstrual bleeding)
Cold clammy skin, rapid weak pulse (shock)
Fever defervescence with clinical worsening (critical phase)

questions.q: When did the fever start, and has it been continuous or come and go?
questions.purpose: Establish day of illness - critical for dengue phase assessment

questions.q: Do you have severe headache, pain behind the eyes, or muscle/joint pain?
Have you noticed any rash, bleeding gums, nosebleeds, or unusual bruising?
questions.purpose: Screen for warning signs of bleeding tendency

questions.q: Have you had persistent vomiting or severe abdominal pain?
questions.purpose: WHO warning sign for progression to severe dengue

questions.q: Has your fever suddenly gone down, and if so, how are you feeling now?
questions.purpose: Assess for critical phase, when plasma leakage risk is highest

questions.q: Has anyone nearby recently had a similar illness with high fever and body aches?
How much are you able to drink, and how often are you urinating?
questions.purpose: Assess hydration and early shock signs

questions.q: Have you had a similar illness with high fever and body aches before?
questions.purpose: Prior infection raises risk of more severe secondary dengue

diseases.context_note: Endemic in Indonesia, especially Java, linked to contaminated food/water; frequent cause of prolonged fever in OPD.
red_flags: Severe abdominal pain with rigidity (possible perforation)
Persistent high fever >7 days unresponsive to treatment

questions.q: How long have you had fever, and does it tend to rise through the day/week?
questions.purpose: Typhoid classically shows a stepwise fever pattern over days

questions.q: Do you have abdominal pain, constipation, or diarrhea?
Have you eaten food from street vendors or unclean water sources recently?
Do you have a headache, loss of appetite, or generally feel very unwell?
Has anyone around you had a similar prolonged fever recently?
Have you taken any antibiotics already for this illness?
questions.purpose: Assess partial treatment, may affect test results and choice of therapy

questions.q: Have you had a similar prolonged fever illness before?
questions.purpose: Assess for relapse or chronic carrier state

questions.q: Do you have severe abdominal pain or notice blood in your stool?
questions.purpose: Screen for intestinal perforation/bleeding - a surgical emergency

diseases.context_note: Common chronic respiratory OPD presentation, aggravated by Java's air pollution, dust, and humidity/mold triggers.
symptoms: Symptoms triggered by exercise, cold air, or allergens

questions.q: How often do you experience wheezing, breathlessness, or chest tightness?
questions.purpose: Assess symptom frequency for control classification

questions.q: Do symptoms wake you up at night, and how often?
What triggers your symptoms - exercise, cold air, dust, smoke, or specific allergens?
Do you or does anyone in your family have a history of wheezing, breathing problems, eczema, or allergies?
Are you currently using any inhaled medication for breathing? How often do you use it?
questions.purpose: Assess current management and technique needs

questions.q: How many times have you needed hospital treatment or been admitted for breathing problems?
questions.purpose: Assess severity and prior exacerbation history

questions.q: Does your breathlessness limit your daily activities or work?
Do you smoke, or are you exposed to smoke/biomass fuel at home?

diseases.context_note: A leading cause of respiratory OPD/ER presentation and hospitalization risk, especially in young children and elderly in Java.
red_flags: Very young or elderly with high fever and rapid breathing

questions.q: How long have you had cough and fever, and is the cough productive?
What color is the sputum, and have you coughed up any blood?
questions.purpose: Assess for bacterial infection or complications

questions.q: Do you have chest pain that worsens with breathing or coughing?
Are you breathing faster than usual, or feeling short of breath at rest?
Do you have any chronic lung disease, heart disease, diabetes, or are you elderly/very young?
questions.purpose: Identify risk factors for severe disease

questions.q: Have you felt confused, extremely weak, or unable to carry out normal activities?
questions.purpose: Screen for severity markers requiring hospitalization

questions.q: Have you had a flu or COVID-like illness recently before these symptoms started?

diseases.context_note: Extremely common OPD complaint across Java puskesmas ('maag'/'sakit lambung'), often overlapping with dyspepsia.
symptoms: Pain related to meals (before or after eating)

questions.q: Where is the pain located, and does eating make it better or worse?
questions.purpose: Differentiate gastric vs duodenal ulcer pattern

questions.q: How long have you had this pain, and is it a new problem or recurring?
Do you take NSAIDs (like ibuprofen), aspirin, or steroids regularly?
questions.purpose: Identify mucosal irritant use, major risk factor

questions.q: Have you vomited blood, or noticed black/tarry stools?
questions.purpose: Screen for GI bleeding - red flag

questions.q: Do you smoke or drink alcohol or coffee frequently?
Have you ever been tested for a stomach infection before, or does anyone in your family have a history of stomach problems or stomach cancer?
Have you lost weight unintentionally or had difficulty swallowing?
questions.purpose: Screen for alarm features requiring endoscopy referral

diseases.context_note: Common complaint related to diet (spicy/fatty food), obesity trends, and late-night eating habits.
symptoms: Worse when lying down or after large meals
red_flags: Chest pain that could mimic cardiac origin

questions.q: Do you feel a burning sensation rising from your stomach to your chest or throat?
Are symptoms worse after eating, lying down, or bending over?
Do you have a sour or bitter taste in your mouth, especially in the morning?
Do you have any difficulty or pain when swallowing food?
Have you noticed a chronic cough, hoarseness, or throat clearing?
What is your typical diet like - fatty, spicy, or large late-night meals?
Have you gained weight recently, and do you smoke?
Could this chest discomfort be related to your heart - do you have exertional chest pain?
questions.purpose: Rule out cardiac cause of chest symptoms

diseases.context_note: Common in older OPD patients, especially knee OA, related to age, obesity, and physical labor.
red_flags: Joint pain with fever/redness (rule out septic arthritis)

questions.q: Which joints are affected, and is the pain worse with activity or at rest?
questions.purpose: Confirm mechanical pattern typical of OA

questions.q: How long does morning stiffness last?
questions.purpose: Differentiate OA (<30 min) from inflammatory arthritis (>1 hour)

questions.q: Do you hear or feel grinding/clicking in the joint when you move it?
questions.purpose: Assess for crepitus, supportive of OA

questions.q: How long have you had these symptoms, and are they getting progressively worse?
Does the joint pain limit your daily activities, walking, or work?
What is your weight and activity/occupation history (e.g., heavy lifting, prolonged standing)?
Have you had any previous joint injury or surgery?
Is there any redness, warmth, or swelling that came on suddenly?
questions.purpose: Rule out an acute inflammatory or infectious process

diseases.context_note: Very common self-reported complaint ('asam urat') in Java OPD, linked to diet high in purines (organ meat, seafood, melinjo).
symptoms: Sudden severe joint pain (classically big toe)
Extreme tenderness (even light touch is painful)
red_flags: Fever with joint swelling (rule out septic arthritis)
Multiple joints involved with systemic symptoms

questions.q: Which joint is affected, and did the pain come on suddenly, often overnight?
questions.purpose: Classic acute gout presentation, especially first MTP joint

questions.q: Have you had similar episodes before? How often?
Have you had any blood tests done before related to joint pain, and were you told about any high levels?
What foods do you eat regularly - organ meats, seafood, melinjo/emping, alcohol (especially beer)?
Do you have fever or feel systemically unwell along with the joint pain?
questions.purpose: Screen for septic arthritis as differential

questions.q: Are you currently on any regular medication for joint pain or previous joint swelling, and do you take it consistently?
questions.purpose: Assess adherence, note starting/stopping can trigger flares

questions.q: Do you have kidney disease or take diuretics?
questions.purpose: Identify factors that raise uric acid/reduce excretion

questions.q: Have you noticed any hard lumps under the skin near your joints?
questions.purpose: Screen for tophi indicating chronic gout

diseases.context_note: Less common than OA/gout but an important differential when patients present with 'rematik' - symmetric small joint disease.
symptoms: Symmetric joint pain and swelling (hands, wrists, feet)
red_flags: Signs of vasculitis (skin ulcers, nerve symptoms)
Sudden neck pain with neurological symptoms (cervical spine involvement)

questions.q: Which joints are affected, and are both sides of the body involved symmetrically?
questions.purpose: Symmetric small joint involvement is characteristic of RA

questions.q: How long does your morning stiffness last?
questions.purpose: >1 hour supports inflammatory arthritis over OA

questions.q: How long have you had these symptoms - weeks, months, or longer?
Do you have fatigue, low-grade fever, or unintentional weight loss?
Does anyone in your family have a history of long-term joint problems or immune-related conditions?
Have you noticed any joint deformity or difficulty with fine hand movements?
Have you had any skin rashes, dry eyes/mouth, or other symptoms besides joint pain?

diseases.context_note: One of the most frequent standalone OPD complaints ('sakit kepala'); usually primary headache disorder.
symptoms: Unilateral throbbing pain, nausea, light/sound sensitivity (migraine)
red_flags: 'Worst headache of life', sudden thunderclap onset
Headache with vomiting and altered consciousness
New headache pattern in patient >50 years

questions.q: Can you describe the pain - is it a tight band-like pressure, or throbbing/pulsating?
Is the pain on one side or both sides of the head?
questions.purpose: Migraine often unilateral; tension usually bilateral

questions.q: Do you have nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light/sound with the headache?
How often do these headaches occur, and how long do they last?
questions.purpose: Assess frequency for chronic vs episodic classification

questions.q: Did this headache come on suddenly and severely, unlike your usual headaches?
Do you have fever, neck stiffness, vision changes, weakness, or confusion?
questions.purpose: Screen for secondary/dangerous causes (meningitis, stroke, mass)

questions.q: What seems to trigger your headaches - stress, lack of sleep, certain foods, menstrual cycle?
How often do you take painkillers for headaches?

diseases.context_note: Very common OPD complaint ('pusing berputar'); important to distinguish peripheral (benign) from central (dangerous) causes.
symptoms: Sudden spinning sensation triggered by head/position change
red_flags: Sudden severe vertigo with new neurological symptoms (weakness, slurred speech, double vision, difficulty walking)
Hearing loss with vertigo (consider vestibular emergency)

questions.q: Does the room spin, or do you feel more like you're going to faint/lightheaded?
What triggers the spinning sensation - specific head movements or position changes (rolling in bed, looking up)?
How long does each episode last - seconds, minutes, or hours?
questions.purpose: BPPV episodes are typically brief (<1 minute)

questions.q: Do you have any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or ear fullness?
questions.purpose: Screen for Meniere's disease or other inner ear pathology

questions.q: Have you had any weakness, slurred speech, double vision, or difficulty walking along with the dizziness?
questions.purpose: Screen for central (stroke-related) cause - red flag

questions.q: Do you have nausea or vomiting with the episodes?
Have you had similar episodes before, and did they resolve on their own?
Do you have high blood pressure, diabetes, or heart disease?
questions.purpose: Assess vascular risk factors relevant to central causes

diseases.context_note: Extremely common complaint, often related to occupation (lifting, prolonged sitting/standing), especially among laborers and market workers.
symptoms: Dull or aching lower back pain
red_flags: Pain radiating down the leg with numbness/weakness (possible nerve compression)
Loss of bladder/bowel control (cauda equina - emergency)
Pain worse at night/unrelieved by rest

questions.q: When did the pain start, and was there a specific triggering event (lifting, injury, prolonged activity)?
Does the pain radiate down your leg, and is there any numbness, tingling, or weakness?
Have you had any loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness in the groin area?
questions.purpose: Screen for cauda equina syndrome - surgical emergency

questions.q: Is the pain worse at night or unrelieved by rest?
questions.purpose: Red flag for infection, malignancy, or inflammatory cause

questions.q: Do you have fever, unexplained weight loss, or a history of cancer?
What is your occupation, and does it involve heavy lifting or prolonged sitting/standing?
Have you had similar back pain episodes before?
What movements or positions make the pain better or worse?
questions.purpose: Assess mechanical pattern to guide management

diseases.context_note: Common in women of reproductive age and children in Java; linked to nutrition and menstrual blood loss.
symptoms: Pica (craving non-food items like ice or dirt)
red_flags: Severe symptomatic anemia (chest pain, severe breathlessness)
Signs of active GI bleeding (melena, hematemesis)

questions.q: How long have you felt tired, weak, or short of breath?
For women: are your menstrual periods heavy or prolonged?
questions.purpose: Identify major cause of iron deficiency in reproductive-age women

questions.q: Have you noticed any blood in your stool, or black tarry stools?
questions.purpose: Screen for occult GI blood loss

questions.q: What does your typical diet look like - do you eat meat, iron-rich vegetables regularly?
Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?
Do you have any craving for unusual substances like ice, dirt, or starch?
questions.purpose: Screen for pica, a classic iron-deficiency symptom

questions.q: Have you had any parasites in your stool before, or lived in an area with poor sanitation and soil contact?
questions.purpose: Assess for hookworm-related blood loss, relevant in rural Java

questions.q: Have you had a blood count test done before, and if so, were you told the results?

diseases.context_note: Growing OPD burden secondary to poorly controlled hypertension and diabetes across Java.

questions.q: Do you have a history of diabetes or hypertension, and how well controlled are they?
questions.purpose: Identify the two leading causes of CKD

questions.q: Have you noticed any swelling in your legs, face, or around your eyes?
Have you noticed foamy/frothy urine, or a change in how much you urinate?
questions.purpose: Screen for proteinuria and renal function changes

questions.q: Do you take painkillers (NSAIDs) frequently, or any herbal/jamu remedies regularly?
questions.purpose: Identify nephrotoxic exposures common in self-medication practices

questions.q: Does anyone in your family have a history of kidney-related health problems?
questions.purpose: Assess genetic risk (e.g., polycystic kidney disease)

questions.q: Have you had any blood or urine tests done before that were flagged as abnormal?
Do you feel unusually tired, itchy, or have poor appetite?
Have you ever had kidney stones, urinary infections, or blockage problems?

diseases.context_note: Common in older patients with smoking history or biomass fuel/cooking smoke exposure, a notable exposure in rural Java kitchens.
red_flags: Chest pain suggestive of cardiac event

questions.q: Do you have a long-standing cough with phlegm, and for how many years?
questions.purpose: Assess chronic bronchitis pattern (cough >3 months/year for 2+ years)

questions.q: Do you smoke, or have you smoked in the past? How many years/packs?
Are you exposed to cooking smoke from wood/biomass fuel, or workplace dust/fumes?
questions.purpose: Identify non-smoking risk factors relevant in rural Java households

questions.q: How far can you walk before feeling breathless, and has this changed over time?
How many times in the past year have you had a flare-up needing extra medication or hospital visits?
questions.purpose: Assess exacerbation frequency for severity classification

questions.q: Did you have breathing problems or wheezing as a child?
Are you currently using any inhalers, and do you know how to use them correctly?
Have you had any swelling in your legs or unusual fatigue?
questions.purpose: Screen for cor pulmonale/right heart strain

diseases.context_note: Common recurring complaint, often mistaken for chronic 'colds'; triggered by dust mites, humidity, and pollution in Java's climate.
red_flags: Symptoms with facial pain/swelling and fever (possible sinusitis)
Unilateral nasal symptoms with bleeding (rule out structural/other cause)

questions.q: How long have you had these symptoms, and do they come and go or are they constant?
What seems to trigger your symptoms - dust, cold air, pets, specific seasons, or environments?
Do you have itchy eyes, throat, or skin along with the nasal symptoms?
Does anyone in your family have a history of sneezing/nasal sensitivity, skin sensitivity, or other allergic-type reactions?
Is the discharge clear and watery, or thick and colored?
Do symptoms affect your sleep or daily activities?
Have you tried any over-the-counter medication for this? Did it help?

diseases.context_note: Common in Java's hot, humid climate; frequently aggravated by sweating, soaps, and occupational exposures.
symptoms: Distribution often in flexural areas (atopic) or contact sites
red_flags: Signs of secondary bacterial infection (pus, spreading redness, fever)

questions.q: Where on the body is the rash, and is it itchy?
Have you started using any new soap, detergent, cosmetic, or come into contact with a new substance recently?
Do you or your family have a history of sensitive skin, breathing problems, or allergic-type reactions?
How long have you had this rash, and has it happened before in the same pattern?
Does sweating, heat, or certain fabrics make it worse?
questions.purpose: Identify aggravating factors relevant to tropical climate

questions.q: Is there any oozing, pus, or increasing redness and warmth?
What have you used to treat it so far, including any topical steroids?

diseases.context_note: Common in crowded households, boarding schools (pesantren), and dormitories across Java due to close contact transmission.
symptoms: Small papules/burrows, often between fingers, wrists, groin
Similar symptoms in close contacts/family members
red_flags: Widespread crusted lesions (possible crusted/Norwegian scabies, seen in immunocompromised)
Signs of secondary bacterial infection (pus, fever, spreading cellulitis)

questions.q: Where is the itching worst, and is it worse at night?
questions.purpose: Classic distribution (finger webs, wrists, groin) and nocturnal itch pattern

questions.q: Does anyone else in your household, dormitory, or close contacts have similar itching?
questions.purpose: Assess for common exposure - scabies spreads with close contact

questions.q: Can you see small burrow lines or tiny bumps on the skin?
How long have you had the itching, and has it been getting worse?
Do you live in a crowded setting such as a boarding school, dormitory, or shared housing?
Have you shared clothing, bedding, or towels with someone who has similar symptoms?
Is there any pus, crusting, or spreading redness at the itchy sites?
questions.purpose: Screen for secondary bacterial skin infection

diseases.name_id: Tinea / Infeksi Jamur Kulit (Panu, Kadas, Kurap)
diseases.context_note: Very common in Java's hot, humid climate; includes tinea corporis, cruris, pedis, and pityriasis versicolor ('panu').
symptoms: Itchy, ring-shaped rash with central clearing
red_flags: Signs of extensive/refractory infection in an immunocompromised patient

questions.q: Where is the rash located, and does it have a ring-like shape with a clearer center?
Is the area itchy, and does sweating or heat make it worse?
questions.purpose: Assess symptom pattern relevant to tropical climate

questions.q: How long have you had this rash, and has it spread?
Do you share clothing, towels, or have close contact with pets or others with similar skin issues?
Have you used any antifungal or steroid creams already? Did symptoms improve or worsen?
questions.purpose: Assess prior treatment - steroid use can worsen tinea (tinea incognito)

questions.q: Do you have diabetes or any condition affecting your immune system?
questions.purpose: Identify risk factors for more extensive/recurrent infection

questions.q: Do you sweat heavily or wear tight/non-breathable clothing for long periods (e.g., for work)?

diseases.context_note: Common OPD complaint, especially among women; recurrent cases seen with poor hydration/hygiene practices.
red_flags: Fever with flank/back pain and vomiting (possible pyelonephritis)
Signs of sepsis (confusion, low blood pressure)
Male with recurrent UTI (may indicate structural abnormality)

questions.q: Do you have burning or pain when urinating, and how often are you urinating?
Do you have any fever, chills, or pain in your back/flank?
questions.purpose: Screen for upper tract involvement (pyelonephritis) - red flag

questions.q: Have you noticed blood or cloudiness in your urine, or an unusual smell?
questions.purpose: Assess for hematuria and infection severity

questions.q: Is there a chance you could be pregnant?
questions.purpose: Pregnancy changes management urgency and antibiotic choice

questions.q: Have you had similar symptoms - burning or frequent urination - before? How often does this happen?
questions.purpose: Assess for recurrent UTI requiring further workup

questions.q: How much water do you drink daily, and do you tend to hold your urine for long periods?
Do you have diabetes or any condition affecting your immune system?
questions.purpose: Identify risk factors for complicated UTI

questions.q: For men: any history of prostate problems or difficulty with urine flow?
questions.purpose: Assess for structural/obstructive cause in male UTI

diseases.context_note: Common, especially in children, often following upper respiratory infections; frequent OPD presentation across Java.
symptoms: In infants: irritability, ear-pulling, poor feeding
red_flags: High fever with lethargy/neck stiffness (possible meningitis)

questions.q: Do you have ear pain, and is it in one ear or both?
Have you noticed any discharge from the ear?
Do you have fever or reduced hearing?
Did this start after a cold or upper respiratory infection?
For a child: has the child been pulling at the ear, unusually irritable, or feeding poorly?
questions.purpose: Assess indirect symptoms in young children who cannot verbalize pain

questions.q: Is there any swelling or tenderness behind the ear?
questions.purpose: Screen for mastoiditis, a serious complication

questions.q: Has water entered the ear recently (swimming, bathing)?
questions.purpose: Assess for otitis externa as an alternative diagnosis

diseases.context_note: Very frequent OPD complaint ('radang tenggorokan'), ranked among top diagnoses at multiple Java puskesmas.
symptoms: Red/swollen tonsils, possibly with white patches
red_flags: Muffled ('hot potato') voice with severe throat pain (possible peritonsillar abscess/epiglottitis)

questions.q: How long have you had the sore throat, and how severe is the pain when swallowing?
Do you have fever, and how high?
Have you noticed any white or yellow patches on your tonsils?
Do you have swollen or tender glands in your neck?
Do you have any difficulty breathing, swallowing your saliva, or opening your mouth wide?
questions.purpose: Screen for airway-threatening complications - red flag

questions.q: Have you been in contact with anyone with a similar sore throat recently?
How often do you get throat infections like this in a year?
questions.purpose: Assess for recurrent tonsillitis needing ENT referral

diseases.context_note: Common, often viral or bacterial, spreads easily in schools/households; frequent 'mata merah' complaint in OPD.
red_flags: Photophobia with headache (possible more serious eye/CNS condition)
History of trauma or foreign body
Contact lens wearer with red painful eye (risk of keratitis)

questions.q: Is one eye affected or both, and did it start in one eye and spread to the other?
questions.purpose: Assess laterality/spread pattern, relevant for viral vs bacterial vs allergic

questions.q: What does the discharge look like - watery, or thick and yellow/green?
Is there any eye pain, or just itching/irritation?
questions.purpose: Significant pain is a red flag requiring urgent eye assessment

questions.q: Have you noticed any change in your vision?
questions.purpose: Screen for vision-threatening conditions requiring urgent referral

questions.q: Are you sensitive to light?
questions.purpose: Photophobia may indicate more serious ocular involvement

questions.q: Has anyone around you had similar red/itchy eyes recently?
questions.purpose: Assess for contagious spread, common with viral conjunctivitis

questions.q: Do you wear contact lenses, or have you had any injury or object in the eye?
questions.purpose: Identify risk factors for more serious corneal involvement

questions.q: Do you have any seasonal allergies, or does this kind of red/itchy eye happen to you at certain times of year?

diseases.context_note: Endemic in parts of Java (e.g., southern coastal areas of Central/East Java, Banten) - important differential for fever in relevant areas/travelers.

questions.q: Do you live in or have you recently traveled to an area known for mosquito-borne fever illness (e.g., southern coastal Java, other islands)?
questions.purpose: Establish exposure risk - essential for malaria suspicion

questions.q: Does your fever come in cycles with chills/shivering followed by sweating?
questions.purpose: Assess for classic paroxysmal fever pattern

questions.q: Have you had a similar fever-with-chills illness before, and did you receive treatment for it?
Do you sleep under a mosquito net, or use mosquito repellent?
Have you noticed yellowing of your eyes/skin, dark urine, or confusion?
questions.purpose: Screen for severe/complicated malaria - red flags

questions.q: Have you already started any treatment for this fever?
questions.purpose: Assess prior treatment, guides further management

questions.q: Do you have a headache, muscle aches, or feel extremely fatigued?

diseases.context_note: Mosquito-borne outbreaks occur periodically across Java; often confused clinically with dengue.
symptoms: Fatigue that can persist for weeks
red_flags: Signs of dengue co-infection (bleeding, warning signs)

questions.q: When did the fever start, and how severe is your joint pain?
questions.purpose: Establish onset and hallmark symptom severity

questions.q: Which joints are painful, and is the pain symmetric on both sides?
questions.purpose: Chikungunya classically causes severe, often symmetric polyarthralgia

questions.q: Have you noticed any skin rash?
Has anyone nearby recently had a similar illness with fever and severe joint pain?
Do you have any bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or persistent vomiting?
questions.purpose: Screen for dengue warning signs, since co-circulation is common

questions.q: How long has the joint pain lasted?
questions.purpose: Chikungunya joint pain can persist for weeks to months (chronic phase)

questions.q: Have you been able to move around and perform daily activities?
questions.purpose: Assess functional impact of joint symptoms

diseases.context_note: Common especially in children in rural/semi-rural Java, related to sanitation and soil-transmitted helminths (roundworm, whipworm, hookworm).
symptoms: Itchy anus (especially pinworm, worse at night)
red_flags: Signs of intestinal obstruction (severe pain, vomiting, no bowel movement/gas)
Signs of malnutrition/failure to thrive in a child

questions.q: Have you noticed any worms in your stool?
Do you have abdominal pain, bloating, or poor appetite?
For a child: has there been poor weight gain, growth delay, or reduced energy/concentration at school?
questions.purpose: Assess nutritional/developmental impact, key in pediatric cases

questions.q: Is there itching around the anus, especially at night?
Do you or your household typically walk barefoot on soil, or how is your access to clean water and sanitation (toilets)?
Have you taken deworming medication before, and when was the last dose?
Do you eat raw or undercooked meat/fish?
questions.purpose: Assess risk for tapeworm infection specifically

diseases.context_note: Notable risk in Java during flooding season (common in Jakarta and other low-lying Java cities); transmitted via rat urine-contaminated water.
red_flags: Jaundice with abdominal pain (possible Weil's disease - hepatic/renal involvement)
Difficulty breathing or coughing blood (pulmonary hemorrhage)

questions.q: Have you had any recent contact with flood water, or waded through standing water?
questions.purpose: Establish key exposure - critical during Java's flood season

questions.q: Do you have severe muscle pain, especially in your calves?
Have you noticed your eyes look red without discharge?
questions.purpose: Screen for conjunctival suffusion, a hallmark sign

questions.q: Have you noticed yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine?
questions.purpose: Screen for hepatic/renal involvement - red flag for severe disease (Weil's disease)

questions.q: How much are you urinating, and has this changed recently?
Do you work in an environment with exposure to rodents, contaminated water, or agriculture/sanitation work?
Have you had any cough or difficulty breathing?
questions.purpose: Screen for pulmonary hemorrhage, a severe complication

diseases.context_note: Common in areas with limited sanitation infrastructure; periodic outbreaks reported in Java linked to contaminated food/water.
red_flags: Signs of acute liver failure (confusion, severe jaundice, bleeding tendency)
Persistent vomiting/inability to keep fluids down

questions.q: Have you noticed yellowing of your eyes or skin, or dark-colored urine?
questions.purpose: Assess for jaundice, a hallmark sign

questions.q: Do you have nausea, poor appetite, or fatigue?
Have you eaten food from street vendors, shellfish, or water from an uncertain source recently?
Has anyone around you recently had similar symptoms - yellowing of the eyes/skin or fatigue with poor appetite?
Do you have pain in the upper right side of your abdomen?
Have you traveled recently to an area with poor sanitation?
Have you been vaccinated against any liver infections in the past?
Do you drink alcohol, or take any medications that could affect the liver?

diseases.context_note: Stroke is a leading cause of disability in Indonesia; many OPD visits are follow-up care for known stroke patients managing risk factors and rehabilitation.
red_flags: New sudden weakness, facial droop, or speech difficulty (possible new stroke/TIA - emergency)

questions.q: When was your stroke, and what part of your body was affected?
Have you noticed any new or worsening weakness, numbness, or speech difficulty since your last visit?
questions.purpose: Screen for new stroke/TIA or progression - urgent if positive

questions.q: Are you taking your blood pressure, diabetes, and cholesterol medications regularly?
Do you have any difficulty swallowing, or have you had choking episodes while eating?
questions.purpose: Screen for dysphagia and aspiration risk

questions.q: How is your mood - have you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in activities?
questions.purpose: Screen for post-stroke depression, common and under-recognized

questions.q: Are you attending physiotherapy or rehabilitation? How is your progress with mobility?
questions.purpose: Assess rehabilitation engagement and functional recovery

questions.q: Do you smoke, and how is your blood pressure and blood sugar control currently?
questions.purpose: Assess ongoing modifiable risk factors for recurrence

questions.q: Have you had any falls recently?
questions.purpose: Assess safety risk related to balance/gait impairment

revision_note: v1.1: history-taking questions rewritten to remove diagnosis-naming, disease-specific drug/lab-test references, and other diagnosis-suggestive phrasing. Clinical intent/purpose of each question is unchanged. Founder-authorized wording adjustment (2026-08-24): D14 Bronchial Asthma patient question was 'needed emergency treatment or hospitalization' and is now 'needed hospital treatment or been admitted' to satisfy the engine no-urgency-word-in-patient-text gate; clinical intent (prior exacerbation and hospital utilization history) unchanged.
